#!/bin/bash

base_folder="/home/krubics/.config/waybar/images/"
battery=$(cat /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/capacity)
if [ $battery -gt 80 ]; then
  echo "${base_folder}100-percent-pikachu.png"
elif [ $battery -gt 60 ]; then
  echo "${base_folder}80-percent-pikachu.png"
elif [ $battery -gt 40 ]; then
  echo "${base_folder}60-percent-pikachu.png"
elif [ $battery -gt 20 ]; then
  echo "${base_folder}40-percent-pikachu.png"
elif [ $battery -gt 10 ]; then
  echo "${base_folder}20-percent-pikachu.png"
else
  echo "${base_folder}10-percent-pikachu.png"
fi

lastPrompt: Let's convert all my jsonc image modules into use background images styled in css instead just like the pokeball example so we can have a consistent height of all the different pokemon.

aiTitle: Convert JSONC image modules to CSS background images

content.text:
I have a clear picture. Two things worth confirming before I write the plan.

**What I found:** 4 image modules (`image#clock` → dialga, `image#network` → wooper, `image#bluetooth` → magneton, `image#battery` → pikachu via script). The pikachu sprites are 677×200 (~3.4:1) while the others are square, which is exactly why heights don't line up — waybar's `size:` is a bounding box, so `size:32` on a square gives 32px tall but `size:115` on pikachu gives only 34px tall. Also: `pickachu-battery.sh` echoes three filenames that don't exist on disk (`80-percent-pikachu.png` vs actual `80-percent-pickachu.png`, `60-percent-pikachi.png`, `10-percent-pickachu.png`), so half your battery sprites are silently broken today.

The CSS conversion can fix all of that, and for battery it can replace the script entirely with waybar's built-in `states` → CSS classes.

questions.question: For the battery pikachu, which approach do you want?

options.label: battery#icon + states (Recommended)
options.description: Add a second battery module `battery#icon` with `format: " "` and a `states` map (p10/p20/p40/p60/p80/p100). Waybar puts a CSS class on the widget, and CSS picks the sprite. Deletes pickachu-battery.sh entirely and fixes the 3 broken filenames as a side effect. Also gives you free `.charging`/`.discharging` classes.

options.label: Keep the script

input.content:
# Convert waybar `image` modules to CSS `background-image`

## Context

The waybar config uses four native `image` modules (`image#clock`, `image#network`,
`image#bluetooth`, `image#battery`) to render pokemon sprites. Waybar's `image` module
sizes via a single `size:` value that acts as a **bounding box**, not a height. Because
the sprites have different aspect ratios, the rendered heights don't match:

| Module | Sprite | Intrinsic size | Aspect | `size:` | Rendered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image#clock` | `dialga.png` | 800×800 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#network` | `pixelated-wooper.png` | 256×256 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#bluetooth` | `pixelated-magneton.png` | 364×364 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#battery` | `*-percent-pikachu.png` | 677×200 | 3.385:1 | 115 | 115×**34** |

The pokeball (`style.css:22-35`) already demonstrates the fix: a CSS `background-image`
on a normal label/button, with the box sized explicitly. That decouples height from
aspect ratio, so every sprite can share one height.

**Outcome:** all five images (four pokemon + pokeball) render at a uniform **26px** tall,
driven entirely from `style.css`. Sprite selection for battery moves from "script echoes
a file path" to "script echoes a CSS class".

Three incidental problems get fixed along the way:

1. **`pickachu-battery.sh` is half-broken today.** It echoes `80-percent-pikachu.png`,
   `60-percent-pikachu.png`, and `10-percent-pikachu.png`, but the files on disk are
   `80-percent-pickachu.png`, `60-percent-pikachi.png`, and `10-percent-pickachu.png`.
   Three of six battery states silently render nothing.
2. **Orphaned icons.** `network` hides itself when disconnected and `bluetooth` hides
   when disabled, but `image#network` / `image#bluetooth` stay onscreen regardless.
3. **Duplicate JSON key.** `config.jsonc:79-80` defines `"format-disconnected"` twice.

---

## Decisions (confirmed with user)

- Battery keeps its script, rewritten to emit JSON (`{"text":" ","class":"p80"}`) instead of a file path.
- Uniform icon height: **26px**. Bar `height` goes 34 → 38.
- Icons hide whenever their sibling module hides.
- Tooltips disabled on every module.
- All images consolidated into `assets/` and renamed consistently.

---

## Step 1 — Consolidate and rename image assets

Everything is CSS-referenced after this change, so the `images/` vs `assets/` split
stops meaning anything. Move all sprites into `assets/` and delete `images/`.

```
images/dialga.png                → assets/dialga.png
images/pixelated-wooper.png      → assets/wooper.png
images/pixelated-magneton.png    → assets/magneton.png
images/100-percent-pikachu.png   → assets/pikachu-100.png
images/80-percent-pickachu.png   → assets/pikachu-80.png
images/60-percent-pikachi.png    → assets/pikachu-60.png
images/40-percent-pikachu.png    → assets/pikachu-40.png
images/20-percent-pikachu.png    → assets/pikachu-20.png
images/10-percent-pickachu.png   → assets/pikachu-10.png
assets/pixelated-pokeball.png    → assets/pokeball.png
```

Use `git mv`-style `mv` (this directory is not a git repo, so plain `mv`), then
`rmdir images/`.

---

## Step 2 — Rewrite `scripts/pickachu-battery.sh`

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh`

Emit waybar JSON instead of a path. `text` must be a single space — waybar's custom
module hides the widget when `text` is empty, and the space is what the background
image paints behind.

Requirements:

- `set -euo pipefail`, `#!/usr/bin/env bash`.
- Read `/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/capacity`. If the file is missing or unreadable,
  log to stderr and emit an empty `text` so the module hides rather than showing a
  stale sprite.
- Allow `WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY` to override the sysfs read. This is what makes the
  six states testable without draining a battery (see Verification).
- Log the resolved capacity and chosen class to stderr with a timestamp; waybar
  surfaces stderr in its own log, and stdout stays clean JSON.
- Same thresholds as today, so behavior is unchanged:

  | Capacity | Class |
  |---|---|
  | `> 80` | `p100` |
  | `> 60` | `p80` |
  | `> 40` | `p60` |
  | `> 20` | `p40` |
  | `> 10` | `p20` |
  | else | `p10` |

- Output exactly: `{"text":" ","class":"<class>"}`

Note the `text` value carries no `%` or capacity — the existing `battery` text module
still renders `{capacity}%` next to it.

---

## Step 3 — Rework `config.jsonc`

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/config.jsonc`

### 3a. Bar height

`"height": 34` → `"height": 38`.

Box math per icon: 26px content + 2px padding × 2 + 4px margin × 2 = 38px.

### 3b. Replace the four `image#*` modules

Delete `image#clock`, `image#network`, `image#bluetooth`, `image#battery` entirely.
Replace them in `modules-left` / `modules-right` at the **same positions** (note
`image#battery` currently sits *after* the `battery` text module — preserve that):

| Old | New | Widget selector | Hides when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image#clock` | `custom/clock-icon` | `#custom-clock-icon` | never |
| `image#network` | `network#icon` | `#network.icon` | disconnected |
| `image#bluetooth` | `bluetooth#icon` | `#bluetooth.icon` | disabled |
| `image#battery` | `custom/battery-icon` | `#custom-battery-icon` | sysfs read fails |

**`custom/clock-icon`** — a static label, no `exec`. This mirrors the existing
`custom/divider` (`config.jsonc:41-43`), which already proves a `custom/` module with
only a `format` works:

```jsonc
"custom/clock-icon": {
  "format": " ",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

**`network#icon`** — reusing the built-in `network` module (rather than a static
`custom/` one) is what makes the wooper disappear alongside the network text. An empty
`format-disconnected` is the same mechanism the existing `network` module already uses
to hide itself.

```jsonc
"network#icon": {
  "interface": "wlo1",
  "format": " ",
  "format-wifi": " ",
  "format-ethernet": " ",
  "format-disconnected": "",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

**`bluetooth#icon`** — same idea, keyed on `format-disabled`:

```jsonc
"bluetooth#icon": {
  "format": " ",
  "format-connected": " ",
  "format-disabled": "",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

The `#icon` suffix becomes a CSS class on the widget. This is the same mechanism
`hyprland/workspaces#taskbar` already relies on for its `#workspaces.taskbar` selector
(`style.css:43`), so it's a pattern already proven in this config.

**`custom/battery-icon`**:

```jsonc
"custom/battery-icon": {
  "exec": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh",
  "return-type": "json",
  "interval": 30,
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

### 3c. Disable tooltips everywhere

Waybar has no global tooltip switch — it's per-module. Add `"tooltip": false` to
`clock`, `network`, `bluetooth`, `battery`, `hyprland/workspaces`,
`hyprland/workspaces#taskbar`, `custom/divider`, `custom/taskbar-divider`, and the four
new icon modules.

Leave the existing `tooltip-format*` keys in place. They become inert, but keeping them
means flipping `"tooltip": true` later restores the old text with no rework.

### 3d. Fix the duplicate key

`config.jsonc:79-80` declares `"format-disconnected"` twice inside `network`. Drop the
first (the one carrying the `//An empty format will hide the module.` comment) and keep
one declaration, preserving the comment.

---

## Step 4 — Add the CSS

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css`

Reuse the exact pattern from the existing pokeball rule (`style.css:22-35`):
`background-image` + `no-repeat` + `center` + `contain` + `background-origin: content-box`,
with the box sized by `min-width` / `min-height`.

`background-size: contain` fits the sprite *inside* the content box, so the rendered
height is `min(box_height, box_width / aspect)`. For height to actually land on 26px,
each box must be at least `26 × aspect` wide:

| Selector | Sprite | Aspect | `min-width` | `min-height` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#custom-clock-icon` | `dialga.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#network.icon` | `wooper.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#bluetooth.icon` | `magneton.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#custom-battery-icon` | `pikachu-*.png` | 3.385:1 | **88px** | 26px |
| `#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active` | `pokeball.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |

Structure it as one shared rule plus per-module `background-image` overrides, so the box
geometry lives in exactly one place:

```css
/* Shared geometry for every CSS-backed sprite. 26px content + 2px padding
   + 4px margin = 38px, matching the bar height. */
#custom-clock-icon,
#network.icon,
#bluetooth.icon,
#custom-battery-icon {
    background-position: center;
    background-repeat: no-repeat;
    background-size: contain;
    background-origin: content-box;
    color: transparent; /* hides the placeholder space glyph */
    min-width: 26px;
    min-height: 26px;
    padding: 2px;
    margin: 4px 0;
}

#custom-clock-icon { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/dialga.png'); }
#network.icon     { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/wooper.png'); }
#bluetooth.icon   { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/magneton.png'); }

/* 26px x 3.385 aspect ratio; contain needs the full width or it letterboxes short */
#custom-battery-icon { min-width: 88px; }

#custom-battery-icon.p100 { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-100.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p80  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-80.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p60  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-60.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p40  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-40.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p20  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-20.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p10  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-10.png'); }
```

Also update the existing pokeball rule: point `background-image` at the renamed
`assets/pokeball.png`, and raise `min-width` / `min-height` from `22px` to `26px` so the
center pill's content height matches the left and right pills.

**Fallback if `contain` misbehaves:** GTK3 also accepts `background-size: auto 26px`,
which pins the height and derives width from the intrinsic aspect ratio. That removes the
dependence on `min-width` being wide enough. Prefer `contain` since it's the pattern
already working in this file; switch only if the pikachu renders letterboxed.

---

## Step 5 — Tune the bar

`height` in waybar is a *request*, not a cap: GTK grows the window when content needs more
room. The `.modules-*` pills add `6px` margin + `4px` padding vertically (20px), so with a
38px icon box the pills want 58px. The bar is already in this state today (the pokeball's
34px box inside those same pills), so this is not a regression — but with icons 4px taller
than before, the bar will grow ~4px.

If the result is too tall, reduce `.modules-left/.modules-center/.modules-right`
`margin: 6px 4px` and `padding: 4px 8px` (`style.css:12-19`) rather than shrinking the
icons. Confirm visually in Step 6 before touching anything.

---

## Verification

1. **Script emits valid JSON for every state.** The `WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY` override
   makes all six branches reachable:
   ```bash
   for c in 95 75 55 35 15 5; do
     WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY=$c /home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh | jq -c .
   done
   ```
   Expect `p100, p80, p60, p40, p20, p10` in order, each with `"text": " "`.

2. **Missing-battery path degrades safely.**
   ```bash
   WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY=  BATTERY_SYSFS=/nonexistent \
     /home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh | jq -c .
   ```
   Expect empty `text` (module hides) plus a stderr log line, and exit 0 — a non-zero exit
   would make waybar spin restarting the module.

3. **Every CSS url resolves.** Guard against typo'd filenames recurring:
   ```bash
   grep -o "url('[^']*')" /home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css \
     | sed "s/url('//;s/')//" | while read -r f; do
         [ -f "$f" ] || echo "MISSING: $f"
       done
   ```
   Expect no output.

4. **Config parses and CSS has no errors.** Run a throwaway instance and read the log:
   ```bash
   waybar -l debug 2>&1 | grep -iE 'error|warning|css'
   ```
   GTK reports unparsed CSS properties here. `background-size: contain` and
   `background-origin` should be silent; anything flagged means falling back to Step 4's
   `auto 26px` form.

5. **Visual check.** Reload the running bar with `killall -SIGUSR2 waybar`, then confirm
   by eye: dialga, wooper, magneton and pikachu all share one height; the pokeball sits at
   the same height; the bar isn't clipped.

6. **Hiding behavior.** Toggle wifi off (`nmcli radio wifi off`) — wooper and the network
   text should both disappear, then both return on `nmcli radio wifi on`. Same for
   `bluetoothctl power off` / `on` and the magneton.

7. **Live battery state.** Unplug AC and watch the sprite change bucket at the 80/60/40/20/10
   boundaries, or just confirm the class is applied now via the running bar's inspector:
   `GTK_DEBUG=interactive waybar`.

---

## Files touched

- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/config.jsonc` — remove 4 `image#*` modules, add 4 icon modules, `height` 34→38, `tooltip: false` everywhere, fix duplicate key
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css` — add shared icon geometry + 9 `background-image` rules, repoint & resize the pokeball rule
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh` — rewrite to emit JSON class, add stderr logging, capacity override, safe fallback
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/` — receives 9 renamed sprites; `pixelated-pokeball.png` → `pokeball.png`
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/images/` — deleted

# Convert waybar `image` modules to CSS `background-image`

## Context

The waybar config uses four native `image` modules (`image#clock`, `image#network`,
`image#bluetooth`, `image#battery`) to render pokemon sprites. Waybar's `image` module
sizes via a single `size:` value that acts as a **bounding box**, not a height. Because
the sprites have different aspect ratios, the rendered heights don't match:

| Module | Sprite | Intrinsic size | Aspect | `size:` | Rendered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image#clock` | `dialga.png` | 800×800 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#network` | `pixelated-wooper.png` | 256×256 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#bluetooth` | `pixelated-magneton.png` | 364×364 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#battery` | `*-percent-pikachu.png` | 677×200 | 3.385:1 | 115 | 115×**34** |

The pokeball (`style.css:22-35`) already demonstrates the fix: a CSS `background-image`
on a normal label/button, with the box sized explicitly. That decouples height from
aspect ratio, so every sprite can share one height.

**Outcome:** all five images (four pokemon + pokeball) render at a uniform **26px** tall,
driven entirely from `style.css`. Sprite selection for battery moves from "script echoes
a file path" to "script echoes a CSS class".

Three incidental problems get fixed along the way:

1. **`pickachu-battery.sh` is half-broken today.** It echoes `80-percent-pikachu.png`,
   `60-percent-pikachu.png`, and `10-percent-pikachu.png`, but the files on disk are
   `80-percent-pickachu.png`, `60-percent-pikachi.png`, and `10-percent-pickachu.png`.
   Three of six battery states silently render nothing.
2. **Orphaned icons.** `network` hides itself when disconnected and `bluetooth` hides
   when disabled, but `image#network` / `image#bluetooth` stay onscreen regardless.
3. **Duplicate JSON key.** `config.jsonc:79-80` defines `"format-disconnected"` twice.

---

## Decisions (confirmed with user)

- Battery keeps its script, rewritten to emit JSON (`{"text":" ","class":"p80"}`) instead of a file path.
- Uniform icon height: **26px**. Bar `height` goes 34 → 38.
- Icons hide whenever their sibling module hides.
- Tooltips disabled on every module.
- All images consolidated into `assets/` and renamed consistently.

---

## Step 1 — Consolidate and rename image assets

Everything is CSS-referenced after this change, so the `images/` vs `assets/` split
stops meaning anything. Move all sprites into `assets/` and delete `images/`.

```
images/dialga.png                → assets/dialga.png
images/pixelated-wooper.png      → assets/wooper.png
images/pixelated-magneton.png    → assets/magneton.png
images/100-percent-pikachu.png   → assets/pikachu-100.png
images/80-percent-pickachu.png   → assets/pikachu-80.png
images/60-percent-pikachi.png    → assets/pikachu-60.png
images/40-percent-pikachu.png    → assets/pikachu-40.png
images/20-percent-pikachu.png    → assets/pikachu-20.png
images/10-percent-pickachu.png   → assets/pikachu-10.png
assets/pixelated-pokeball.png    → assets/pokeball.png
```

This directory is not a git repo, so plain `mv`, then `rmdir images/`.

---

## Step 2 — Rewrite `scripts/pickachu-battery.sh`

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh`

Emit waybar JSON instead of a path. `text` must be a single space — waybar's custom
module hides the widget when `text` is empty, and the space is what the background
image paints behind.

Requirements:

- `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`.
- Read `/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/capacity`. If the file is missing or unreadable,
  log to stderr and emit an empty `text` so the module hides rather than showing a
  stale sprite. Exit 0 regardless — a non-zero exit makes waybar respawn the module.
- Allow `WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY` to override the sysfs read, and `BATTERY_SYSFS` to
  override the path. These are what make all six branches testable without draining a
  battery (see Verification).
- Log the resolved capacity and chosen class to stderr with an ISO-8601 timestamp;
  waybar surfaces stderr in its own log, and stdout stays clean JSON.
- Same thresholds as today, so behavior is unchanged:

  | Capacity | Class |
  |---|---|
  | `> 80` | `p100` |
  | `> 60` | `p80` |
  | `> 40` | `p60` |
  | `> 20` | `p40` |
  | `> 10` | `p20` |
  | else | `p10` |

- Output exactly: `{"text":" ","class":"<class>"}`

The `text` value carries no capacity number — the existing `battery` text module still
renders `{capacity}%` next to it.

---

## Step 3 — Rework `config.jsonc`

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/config.jsonc`

### 3a. Bar height

`"height": 34` → `"height": 38`.

Box math per icon: 26px content + 2px padding × 2 + 4px margin × 2 = 38px.

### 3b. Replace the four `image#*` modules

Delete `image#clock`, `image#network`, `image#bluetooth`, `image#battery` entirely.
Replace them in `modules-left` / `modules-right` at the **same positions** (note
`image#battery` currently sits *after* the `battery` text module — preserve that):

| Old | New | Widget selector | Hides when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image#clock` | `custom/clock-icon` | `#custom-clock-icon` | never |
| `image#network` | `network#icon` | `#network.icon` | disconnected |
| `image#bluetooth` | `bluetooth#icon` | `#bluetooth.icon` | disabled |
| `image#battery` | `custom/battery-icon` | `#custom-battery-icon` | sysfs read fails |

**`custom/clock-icon`** — a static label, no `exec`. This mirrors the existing
`custom/divider` (`config.jsonc:41-43`), which already proves a `custom/` module with
only a `format` works:

```jsonc
"custom/clock-icon": {
  "format": " ",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

**`network#icon`** — reusing the built-in `network` module (rather than a static
`custom/` one) is what makes the wooper disappear alongside the network text. An empty
`format-disconnected` is the same mechanism the existing `network` module already uses
to hide itself.

```jsonc
"network#icon": {
  "interface": "wlo1",
  "format": " ",
  "format-wifi": " ",
  "format-ethernet": " ",
  "format-disconnected": "",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

**`bluetooth#icon`** — same idea, keyed on `format-disabled`:

```jsonc
"bluetooth#icon": {
  "format": " ",
  "format-connected": " ",
  "format-disabled": "",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

The `#icon` suffix becomes a CSS class on the widget. This is the same mechanism
`hyprland/workspaces#taskbar` already relies on for its `#workspaces.taskbar` selector
(`style.css:43`), so the pattern is already proven in this config.

**`custom/battery-icon`**:

```jsonc
"custom/battery-icon": {
  "exec": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh",
  "return-type": "json",
  "interval": 30,
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

### 3c. Disable tooltips everywhere

Waybar has no global tooltip switch — it's per-module. Add `"tooltip": false` to
`clock`, `network`, `bluetooth`, `battery`, `hyprland/workspaces`,
`hyprland/workspaces#taskbar`, `custom/divider`, `custom/taskbar-divider`, and the four
new icon modules.

Leave the existing `tooltip-format*` keys in place. They become inert, but keeping them
means flipping `"tooltip": true` later restores the old text with no rework.

### 3d. Fix the duplicate key

`config.jsonc:79-80` declares `"format-disconnected"` twice inside `network`. Keep one
declaration, preserving the `//An empty format will hide the module.` comment.

---

## Step 4 — Add the CSS

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css`

Reuse the exact pattern from the existing pokeball rule (`style.css:22-35`):
`background-image` + `no-repeat` + `center` + `contain` + `background-origin: content-box`,
with the box sized by `min-width` / `min-height`.

`background-size: contain` fits the sprite *inside* the content box, so rendered height is
`min(box_height, box_width / aspect)`. For height to actually land on 26px, each box must
be at least `26 × aspect` wide:

| Selector | Sprite | Aspect | `min-width` | `min-height` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#custom-clock-icon` | `dialga.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#network.icon` | `wooper.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#bluetooth.icon` | `magneton.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#custom-battery-icon` | `pikachu-*.png` | 3.385:1 | **88px** | 26px |
| `#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active` | `pokeball.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |

Structure it as one shared rule plus per-module `background-image` overrides, so the box
geometry lives in exactly one place:

```css
/* Shared geometry for every CSS-backed sprite. 26px content + 2px padding
   + 4px margin = 38px, matching the bar height. */
#custom-clock-icon,
#network.icon,
#bluetooth.icon,
#custom-battery-icon {
    background-position: center;
    background-repeat: no-repeat;
    background-size: contain;
    background-origin: content-box;
    color: transparent; /* hides the placeholder space glyph */
    min-width: 26px;
    min-height: 26px;
    padding: 2px;
    margin: 4px 0;
}

#custom-clock-icon { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/dialga.png'); }
#network.icon      { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/wooper.png'); }
#bluetooth.icon    { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/magneton.png'); }

/* 26px x 3.385 aspect ratio; contain letterboxes short without the full width */
#custom-battery-icon { min-width: 88px; }

#custom-battery-icon.p100 { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-100.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p80  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-80.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p60  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-60.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p40  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-40.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p20  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-20.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p10  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-10.png'); }
```

Also update the existing pokeball rule: point `background-image` at the renamed
`assets/pokeball.png`, and raise `min-width` / `min-height` from `22px` to `26px` so the
center pill's content height matches the left and right pills.

**Fallback if `contain` misbehaves:** GTK3 also accepts `background-size: auto 26px`,
which pins the height and derives width from the intrinsic aspect ratio, removing the
dependence on `min-width` being wide enough. Prefer `contain` since it's the pattern
already working in this file; switch only if the pikachu renders letterboxed.

---

## Step 5 — Tune the bar

`height` in waybar is a *request*, not a cap: GTK grows the window when content needs more
room. The `.modules-*` pills add `6px` margin + `4px` padding vertically (20px), so with a
38px icon box the pills want 58px. The bar is already in this state today (the pokeball's
34px box inside those same pills), so this is not a regression — but with icons 4px taller
than before, the bar will grow ~4px.

If the result is too tall, reduce `.modules-left/.modules-center/.modules-right`
`margin: 6px 4px` and `padding: 4px 8px` (`style.css:12-19`) rather than shrinking the
icons. Confirm visually in Verification step 5 before touching anything.

---

## Verification

1. **Script emits valid JSON for every state.** The capacity override makes all six
   branches reachable:
   ```bash
   for c in 95 75 55 35 15 5; do
     WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY=$c /home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh | jq -c .
   done
   ```
   Expect `p100, p80, p60, p40, p20, p10` in order, each with `"text": " "`.

2. **Missing-battery path degrades safely.**
   ```bash
   BATTERY_SYSFS=/nonexistent /home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh | jq -c .
   echo "exit=$?"
   ```
   Expect empty `text` (module hides), a stderr log line, and `exit=0`.

3. **Every CSS url resolves.** Guards against typo'd filenames recurring:
   ```bash
   grep -o "url('[^']*')" /home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css \
     | sed "s/url('//;s/')//" | while read -r f; do
         [ -f "$f" ] || echo "MISSING: $f"
   ```

# Convert waybar `image` modules to CSS `background-image`

## Context

The waybar config uses four native `image` modules (`image#clock`, `image#network`,
`image#bluetooth`, `image#battery`) to render pokemon sprites. Waybar's `image` module
sizes via a single `size:` value that acts as a **bounding box**, not a height. Because
the sprites have different aspect ratios, the rendered heights don't match:

| Module | Sprite | Intrinsic size | Aspect | `size:` | Rendered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image#clock` | `dialga.png` | 800×800 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#network` | `pixelated-wooper.png` | 256×256 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#bluetooth` | `pixelated-magneton.png` | 364×364 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#battery` | `*-percent-pikachu.png` | 677×200 | 3.385:1 | 115 | 115×**34** |

The pokeball (`style.css:22-35`) already demonstrates the fix: a CSS `background-image`
on a normal label/button, with the box sized explicitly. That decouples height from
aspect ratio, so every sprite can share one height.

**Outcome:** all five images (four pokemon + pokeball) render at a uniform **26px** tall,
driven entirely from `style.css`. Sprite selection for battery moves from "script echoes
a file path" to "script echoes a CSS class".

Three incidental problems get fixed along the way:

1. **`pickachu-battery.sh` is half-broken today.** It echoes `80-percent-pikachu.png`,
   `60-percent-pikachu.png`, and `10-percent-pikachu.png`, but the files on disk are
   `80-percent-pickachu.png`, `60-percent-pikachi.png`, and `10-percent-pickachu.png`.
   Three of six battery states silently render nothing.
2. **Orphaned icons.** `network` hides itself when disconnected and `bluetooth` hides
   when disabled, but `image#network` / `image#bluetooth` stay onscreen regardless.
3. **Duplicate JSON key.** `config.jsonc:79-80` defines `"format-disconnected"` twice.

---

## Decisions (confirmed with user)

- Battery keeps its script, rewritten to emit JSON (`{"text":" ","class":"p80"}`) instead of a file path.
- Uniform icon height: **26px**. Bar `height` goes 34 → 38.
- Icons hide whenever their sibling module hides.
- Tooltips disabled on every module.
- All images consolidated into `assets/` and renamed consistently.

---

## Step 1 — Consolidate and rename image assets

Everything is CSS-referenced after this change, so the `images/` vs `assets/` split
stops meaning anything. Move all sprites into `assets/` and delete `images/`.

```
images/dialga.png                → assets/dialga.png
images/pixelated-wooper.png      → assets/wooper.png
images/pixelated-magneton.png    → assets/magneton.png
images/100-percent-pikachu.png   → assets/pikachu-100.png
images/80-percent-pickachu.png   → assets/pikachu-80.png
images/60-percent-pikachi.png    → assets/pikachu-60.png
images/40-percent-pikachu.png    → assets/pikachu-40.png
images/20-percent-pikachu.png    → assets/pikachu-20.png
images/10-percent-pickachu.png   → assets/pikachu-10.png
assets/pixelated-pokeball.png    → assets/pokeball.png
```

This directory is not a git repo, so plain `mv`, then `rmdir images/`.

---

## Step 2 — Rewrite `scripts/pickachu-battery.sh`

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh`

Emit waybar JSON instead of a path. `text` must be a single space — waybar's custom
module hides the widget when `text` is empty, and the space is what the background
image paints behind.

Requirements:

- `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`.
- Read `/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/capacity`. If the file is missing or unreadable,
  log to stderr and emit an empty `text` so the module hides rather than showing a
  stale sprite. Exit 0 regardless — a non-zero exit makes waybar respawn the module.
- Allow `WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY` to override the sysfs read, and `BATTERY_SYSFS` to
  override the path. These are what make all six branches testable without draining a
  battery (see Verification).
- Log the resolved capacity and chosen class to stderr with an ISO-8601 timestamp;
  waybar surfaces stderr in its own log, and stdout stays clean JSON.
- Same thresholds as today, so behavior is unchanged:

  | Capacity | Class |
  |---|---|
  | `> 80` | `p100` |
  | `> 60` | `p80` |
  | `> 40` | `p60` |
  | `> 20` | `p40` |
  | `> 10` | `p20` |
  | else | `p10` |

- Output exactly: `{"text":" ","class":"<class>"}`

The `text` value carries no capacity number — the existing `battery` text module still
renders `{capacity}%` next to it.

---

## Step 3 — Rework `config.jsonc`

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/config.jsonc`

### 3a. Bar height

`"height": 34` → `"height": 38`.

Box math per icon: 26px content + 2px padding × 2 + 4px margin × 2 = 38px.

### 3b. Replace the four `image#*` modules

Delete `image#clock`, `image#network`, `image#bluetooth`, `image#battery` entirely.
Replace them in `modules-left` / `modules-right` at the **same positions** (note
`image#battery` currently sits *after* the `battery` text module — preserve that):

| Old | New | Widget selector | Hides when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image#clock` | `custom/clock-icon` | `#custom-clock-icon` | never |
| `image#network` | `network#icon` | `#network.icon` | disconnected |
| `image#bluetooth` | `bluetooth#icon` | `#bluetooth.icon` | disabled |
| `image#battery` | `custom/battery-icon` | `#custom-battery-icon` | sysfs read fails |

**`custom/clock-icon`** — a static label, no `exec`. This mirrors the existing
`custom/divider` (`config.jsonc:41-43`), which already proves a `custom/` module with
only a `format` works:

```jsonc
"custom/clock-icon": {
  "format": " ",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

**`network#icon`** — reusing the built-in `network` module (rather than a static
`custom/` one) is what makes the wooper disappear alongside the network text. An empty
`format-disconnected` is the same mechanism the existing `network` module already uses
to hide itself.

```jsonc
"network#icon": {
  "interface": "wlo1",
  "format": " ",
  "format-wifi": " ",
  "format-ethernet": " ",
  "format-disconnected": "",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

**`bluetooth#icon`** — same idea, keyed on `format-disabled`:

```jsonc
"bluetooth#icon": {
  "format": " ",
  "format-connected": " ",
  "format-disabled": "",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

The `#icon` suffix becomes a CSS class on the widget. This is the same mechanism
`hyprland/workspaces#taskbar` already relies on for its `#workspaces.taskbar` selector
(`style.css:43`), so the pattern is already proven in this config.

**`custom/battery-icon`**:

```jsonc
"custom/battery-icon": {
  "exec": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh",
  "return-type": "json",
  "interval": 30,
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

### 3c. Disable tooltips everywhere

Waybar has no global tooltip switch — it's per-module. Add `"tooltip": false` to
`clock`, `network`, `bluetooth`, `battery`, `hyprland/workspaces`,
`hyprland/workspaces#taskbar`, `custom/divider`, `custom/taskbar-divider`, and the four
new icon modules.

Leave the existing `tooltip-format*` keys in place. They become inert, but keeping them
means flipping `"tooltip": true` later restores the old text with no rework.

### 3d. Fix the duplicate key

`config.jsonc:79-80` declares `"format-disconnected"` twice inside `network`. Keep one
declaration, preserving the `//An empty format will hide the module.` comment.

---

## Step 4 — Add the CSS

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css`

Reuse the exact pattern from the existing pokeball rule (`style.css:22-35`):
`background-image` + `no-repeat` + `center` + `contain` + `background-origin: content-box`,
with the box sized by `min-width` / `min-height`.

`background-size: contain` fits the sprite *inside* the content box, so rendered height is
`min(box_height, box_width / aspect)`. For height to actually land on 26px, each box must
be at least `26 × aspect` wide:

| Selector | Sprite | Aspect | `min-width` | `min-height` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#custom-clock-icon` | `dialga.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#network.icon` | `wooper.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#bluetooth.icon` | `magneton.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#custom-battery-icon` | `pikachu-*.png` | 3.385:1 | **88px** | 26px |
| `#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active` | `pokeball.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |

geometry lives in exactly one place:

```css
/* Shared geometry for every CSS-backed sprite. 26px content + 2px padding
   + 4px margin = 38px, matching the bar height. */
#custom-clock-icon,
#network.icon,
#bluetooth.icon,
#custom-battery-icon {
    background-position: center;
    background-repeat: no-repeat;
    background-size: contain;
    background-origin: content-box;
    color: transparent; /* hides the placeholder space glyph */
    min-width: 26px;
    min-height: 26px;
    padding: 2px;
    margin: 4px 0;
}

#custom-clock-icon { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/dialga.png'); }
#network.icon      { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/wooper.png'); }
#bluetooth.icon    { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/magneton.png'); }

/* 26px x 3.385 aspect ratio; contain letterboxes short without the full width */
#custom-battery-icon { min-width: 88px; }

#custom-battery-icon.p100 { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-100.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p80  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-80.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p60  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-60.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p40  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-40.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p20  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-20.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p10  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-10.png'); }
```

Also update the existing pokeball rule: point `background-image` at the renamed
`assets/pokeball.png`, and raise `min-width` / `min-height` from `22px` to `26px` so the
center pill's content height matches the left and right pills.

**Fallback if `contain` misbehaves:** GTK3 also accepts `background-size: auto 26px`,
which pins the height and derives width from the intrinsic aspect ratio, removing the
dependence on `min-width` being wide enough. Prefer `contain` since it's the pattern
already working in this file; switch only if the pikachu renders letterboxed.

---

## Step 5 — Tune the bar

`height` in waybar is a *request*, not a cap: GTK grows the window when content needs more
room. The `.modules-*` pills add `6px` margin + `4px` padding vertically (20px), so with a
38px icon box the pills want 58px. The bar is already in this state today (the pokeball's
34px box inside those same pills), so this is not a regression — but with icons 4px taller
than before, the bar will grow ~4px.

If the result is too tall, reduce `.modules-left/.modules-center/.modules-right`
`margin: 6px 4px` and `padding: 4px 8px` (`style.css:12-19`) rather than shrinking the
icons. Confirm visually in Verification step 5 before touching anything.

---

## Verification

1. **Script emits valid JSON for every state.** The capacity override makes all six
   branches reachable:
   ```bash
   for c in 95 75 55 35 15 5; do
     WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY=$c /home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh | jq -c .
   done
   ```
   Expect `p100, p80, p60, p40, p20, p10` in order, each with `"text": " "`.

2. **Missing-battery path degrades safely.**
   ```bash
   BATTERY_SYSFS=/nonexistent /home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh | jq -c .
   echo "exit=$?"
   ```
   Expect empty `text` (module hides), a stderr log line, and `exit=0`.

3. **Every CSS url resolves.** Guards against typo'd filenames recurring:
   ```bash
   grep -o "url('[^']*')" /home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css \
     | sed "s/url('//;s/')//" | while read -r f; do
         [ -f "$f" ] || echo "MISSING: $f"
       done
   ```
   Expect no output.

4. **Config parses and CSS has no errors.** Run a throwaway instance and read the log:
   ```bash
   waybar -l debug 2>&1 | grep -iE 'error|warning|css'
   ```
   GTK reports unparsed CSS properties here. `background-size: contain` and
   `background-origin` should be silent; anything flagged means falling back to Step 4's
   `auto 26px` form.

5. **Visual check.** Reload the running bar with `killall -SIGUSR2 waybar`, then confirm by
   eye: dialga, wooper, magneton and pikachu all share one height; the pokeball sits at the
   same height; the bar isn't clipped.

6. **Hiding behavior.** `nmcli radio wifi off` — wooper and the network text should both
   disappear, then both return on `nmcli radio wifi on`. Same for `bluetoothctl power off`
   / `on` and the magneton.

7. **Live battery class.** Inspect the running widget's CSS classes with
   `GTK_DEBUG=interactive waybar`, or unplug AC and watch the sprite change bucket at the
   80/60/40/20/10 boundaries.

---

- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/config.jsonc` — remove 4 `image#*` modules, add 4 icon modules, `height` 34→38, `tooltip: false` everywhere, fix duplicate key
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css` — add shared icon geometry + 9 `background-image` rules, repoint & resize the pokeball rule
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh` — rewrite to emit JSON class, add stderr logging, capacity override, safe fallback
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/` — receives 9 renamed sprites; `pixelated-pokeball.png` → `pokeball.png`
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/images/` — deleted

The waybar config uses four native `image` modules (`image#clock`, `image#network`,

Plan is written. The short version:

All four `image#*` modules become ordinary label modules with a CSS `background-image`, sized by a shared `min-height: 26px` box — which is what finally makes the heights match, since waybar's `size:` was treating the 677×200 pikachu as a bounding box and only ever giving it 34px of height.

Two things I found while exploring that are worth knowing:

**Three of your six battery sprites have never rendered.** `pickachu-battery.sh` echoes `80-percent-pikachu.png`, `60-percent-pikachu.png`, and `10-percent-pikachu.png`, but the files on disk are `80-percent-pi**ck**achu.png`, `60-percent-pika**chi**.png`, and `10-percent-pi**ck**achu.png`. The rename-and-consolidate step you asked for clears this up permanently.

**Your wooper and magneton are orphans.** The `network` and `bluetooth` text modules already hide themselves when disconnected/disabled, but the image modules sitting next to them don't. You asked for the pokemon to hide with their module, so I'm converting those two to `network#icon` and `bluetooth#icon` — real network/bluetooth modules with a blank format and an empty `format-disconnected`/`format-disabled`, which reuses waybar's own hiding mechanism rather than inventing one.

Battery stays on the script as you chose, rewritten to emit `{"text":" ","class":"p80"}` so CSS picks the sprite. I added a `WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY` override so all six buckets are testable without draining a battery.

One caveat I want to flag rather than bury: waybar's `height` is a request, not a cap. Your bar already renders taller than the configured `34` because the pokeball's box plus the pill margins exceed it. Going to 26px icons will grow the bar roughly 4px more. I've set `height: 38` and left the pill margins alone — step 5 of the plan covers trimming them if it looks too tall once you can see it.

input.plan:
# Convert waybar `image` modules to CSS `background-image`

## Context

The waybar config uses four native `image` modules (`image#clock`, `image#network`,
`image#bluetooth`, `image#battery`) to render pokemon sprites. Waybar's `image` module
sizes via a single `size:` value that acts as a **bounding box**, not a height. Because
the sprites have different aspect ratios, the rendered heights don't match:

| Module | Sprite | Intrinsic size | Aspect | `size:` | Rendered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image#clock` | `dialga.png` | 800×800 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#network` | `pixelated-wooper.png` | 256×256 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#bluetooth` | `pixelated-magneton.png` | 364×364 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#battery` | `*-percent-pikachu.png` | 677×200 | 3.385:1 | 115 | 115×**34** |

The pokeball (`style.css:22-35`) already demonstrates the fix: a CSS `background-image`
on a normal label/button, with the box sized explicitly. That decouples height from
aspect ratio, so every sprite can share one height.

**Outcome:** all five images (four pokemon + pokeball) render at a uniform **26px** tall,
driven entirely from `style.css`. Sprite selection for battery moves from "script echoes
a file path" to "script echoes a CSS class".

Three incidental problems get fixed along the way:

1. **`pickachu-battery.sh` is half-broken today.** It echoes `80-percent-pikachu.png`,
   `60-percent-pikachu.png`, and `10-percent-pikachu.png`, but the files on disk are
   `80-percent-pickachu.png`, `60-percent-pikachi.png`, and `10-percent-pickachu.png`.
   Three of six battery states silently render nothing.
2. **Orphaned icons.** `network` hides itself when disconnected and `bluetooth` hides
   when disabled, but `image#network` / `image#bluetooth` stay onscreen regardless.
3. **Duplicate JSON key.** `config.jsonc:79-80` defines `"format-disconnected"` twice.

---

## Decisions (confirmed with user)

- Battery keeps its script, rewritten to emit JSON (`{"text":" ","class":"p80"}`) instead of a file path.
- Uniform icon height: **26px**. Bar `height` goes 34 → 38.
- Icons hide whenever their sibling module hides.
- Tooltips disabled on every module.
- All images consolidated into `assets/` and renamed consistently.

---

## Step 1 — Consolidate and rename image assets

Everything is CSS-referenced after this change, so the `images/` vs `assets/` split
stops meaning anything. Move all sprites into `assets/` and delete `images/`.

```
images/dialga.png                → assets/dialga.png
images/pixelated-wooper.png      → assets/wooper.png
images/pixelated-magneton.png    → assets/magneton.png
images/100-percent-pikachu.png   → assets/pikachu-100.png
images/80-percent-pickachu.png   → assets/pikachu-80.png
images/60-percent-pikachi.png    → assets/pikachu-60.png
images/40-percent-pikachu.png    → assets/pikachu-40.png
images/20-percent-pikachu.png    → assets/pikachu-20.png
images/10-percent-pickachu.png   → assets/pikachu-10.png
assets/pixelated-pokeball.png    → assets/pokeball.png
```

This directory is not a git repo, so plain `mv`, then `rmdir images/`.

---

## Step 2 — Rewrite `scripts/pickachu-battery.sh`

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh`

Emit waybar JSON instead of a path. `text` must be a single space — waybar's custom
module hides the widget when `text` is empty, and the space is what the background
image paints behind.

Requirements:

- `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`.
- Read `/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/capacity`. If the file is missing or unreadable,
  log to stderr and emit an empty `text` so the module hides rather than showing a
  stale sprite. Exit 0 regardless — a non-zero exit makes waybar respawn the module.
- Allow `WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY` to override the sysfs read, and `BATTERY_SYSFS` to
  override the path. These are what make all six branches testable without draining a
  battery (see Verification).
- Log the resolved capacity and chosen class to stderr with an ISO-8601 timestamp;
  waybar surfaces stderr in its own log, and stdout stays clean JSON.
- Same thresholds as today, so behavior is unchanged:

  | Capacity | Class |
  |---|---|
  | `> 80` | `p100` |
  | `> 60` | `p80` |
  | `> 40` | `p60` |
  | `> 20` | `p40` |
  | `> 10` | `p20` |
  | else | `p10` |

- Output exactly: `{"text":" ","class":"<class>"}`

The `text` value carries no capacity number — the existing `battery` text module still
renders `{capacity}%` next to it.

---

## Step 3 — Rework `config.jsonc`

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/config.jsonc`

### 3a. Bar height

`"height": 34` → `"height": 38`.

Box math per icon: 26px content + 2px padding × 2 + 4px margin × 2 = 38px.

### 3b. Replace the four `image#*` modules

Delete `image#clock`, `image#network`, `image#bluetooth`, `image#battery` entirely.
Replace them in `modules-left` / `modules-right` at the **same positions** (note
`image#battery` currently sits *after* the `battery` text module — preserve that):

| Old | New | Widget selector | Hides when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image#clock` | `custom/clock-icon` | `#custom-clock-icon` | never |
| `image#network` | `network#icon` | `#network.icon` | disconnected |
| `image#bluetooth` | `bluetooth#icon` | `#bluetooth.icon` | disabled |
| `image#battery` | `custom/battery-icon` | `#custom-battery-icon` | sysfs read fails |

**`custom/clock-icon`** — a static label, no `exec`. This mirrors the existing
`custom/divider` (`config.jsonc:41-43`), which already proves a `custom/` module with
only a `format` works:

```jsonc
"custom/clock-icon": {
  "format": " ",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

**`network#icon`** — reusing the built-in `network` module (rather than a static
`custom/` one) is what makes the wooper disappear alongside the network text. An empty
`format-disconnected` is the same mechanism the existing `network` module already uses
to hide itself.

```jsonc
"network#icon": {
  "interface": "wlo1",
  "format": " ",
  "format-wifi": " ",
  "format-ethernet": " ",
  "format-disconnected": "",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

**`bluetooth#icon`** — same idea, keyed on `format-disabled`:

```jsonc
"bluetooth#icon": {
  "format": " ",
  "format-connected": " ",
  "format-disabled": "",
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

The `#icon` suffix becomes a CSS class on the widget. This is the same mechanism
`hyprland/workspaces#taskbar` already relies on for its `#workspaces.taskbar` selector
(`style.css:43`), so the pattern is already proven in this config.

**`custom/battery-icon`**:

```jsonc
"custom/battery-icon": {
  "exec": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh",
  "return-type": "json",
  "interval": 30,
  "tooltip": false,
},
```

### 3c. Disable tooltips everywhere

Waybar has no global tooltip switch — it's per-module. Add `"tooltip": false` to
`clock`, `network`, `bluetooth`, `battery`, `hyprland/workspaces`,
`hyprland/workspaces#taskbar`, `custom/divider`, `custom/taskbar-divider`, and the four
new icon modules.

Leave the existing `tooltip-format*` keys in place. They become inert, but keeping them
means flipping `"tooltip": true` later restores the old text with no rework.

### 3d. Fix the duplicate key

`config.jsonc:79-80` declares `"format-disconnected"` twice inside `network`. Keep one
declaration, preserving the `//An empty format will hide the module.` comment.

---

## Step 4 — Add the CSS

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css`

Reuse the exact pattern from the existing pokeball rule (`style.css:22-35`):
`background-image` + `no-repeat` + `center` + `contain` + `background-origin: content-box`,
with the box sized by `min-width` / `min-height`.

`background-size: contain` fits the sprite *inside* the content box, so rendered height is
`min(box_height, box_width / aspect)`. For height to actually land on 26px, each box must
be at least `26 × aspect` wide:

| Selector | Sprite | Aspect | `min-width` | `min-height` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#custom-clock-icon` | `dialga.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#network.icon` | `wooper.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#bluetooth.icon` | `magneton.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#custom-battery-icon` | `pikachu-*.png` | 3.385:1 | **88px** | 26px |
| `#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active` | `pokeball.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |

Structure it as one shared rule plus per-module `background-image` overrides, so the box
geometry lives in exactly one place:

```css
/* Shared geometry for every CSS-backed sprite. 26px content + 2px padding
   + 4px margin = 38px, matching the bar height. */
#custom-clock-icon,
#network.icon,
#bluetooth.icon,
#custom-battery-icon {
    background-position: center;
    background-repeat: no-repeat;
    background-size: contain;
    background-origin: content-box;
    color: transparent; /* hides the placeholder space glyph */
    min-width: 26px;
    min-height: 26px;
    padding: 2px;
    margin: 4px 0;
}

#custom-clock-icon { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/dialga.png'); }
#network.icon      { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/wooper.png'); }
#bluetooth.icon    { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/magneton.png'); }

/* 26px x 3.385 aspect ratio; contain letterboxes short without the full width */
#custom-battery-icon { min-width: 88px; }

#custom-battery-icon.p100 { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-100.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p80  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-80.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p60  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-60.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p40  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-40.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p20  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-20.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p10  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-10.png'); }
```

Also update the existing pokeball rule: point `background-image` at the renamed
`assets/pokeball.png`, and raise `min-width` / `min-height` from `22px` to `26px` so the
center pill's content height matches the left and right pills.

**Fallback if `contain` misbehaves:** GTK3 also accepts `background-size: auto 26px`,
which pins the height and derives width from the intrinsic aspect ratio, removing the
dependence on `min-width` being wide enough. Prefer `contain` since it's the pattern
already working in this file; switch only if the pikachu renders letterboxed.

---

## Step 5 — Tune the bar

`height` in waybar is a *request*, not a cap: GTK grows the window when content needs more
room. The `.modules-*` pills add `6px` margin + `4px` padding vertically (20px), so with a
38px icon box the pills want 58px. The bar is already in this state today (the pokeball's
34px box inside those same pills), so this is not a regression — but with icons 4px taller
than before, the bar will grow ~4px.

## Context

The waybar config uses four native `image` modules (`image#clock`, `image#network`,
`image#bluetooth`, `image#battery`) to render pokemon sprites. Waybar's `image` module
sizes via a single `size:` value that acts as a **bounding box**, not a height. Because
the sprites have different aspect ratios, the rendered heights don't match:

| Module | Sprite | Intrinsic size | Aspect | `size:` | Rendered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image#clock` | `dialga.png` | 800×800 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#network` | `pixelated-wooper.png` | 256×256 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#bluetooth` | `pixelated-magneton.png` | 364×364 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
| `image#battery` | `*-percent-pikachu.png` | 677×200 | 3.385:1 | 115 | 115×**34** |

The pokeball (`style.css:22-35`) already demonstrates the fix: a CSS `background-image`
on a normal label/button, with the box sized explicitly. That decouples height from
aspect ratio, so every sprite can share one height.

**Outcome:** all five images (four pokemon + pokeball) render at a uniform **26px** tall,
driven entirely from `style.css`. Sprite selection for battery moves from "script echoes
a file path" to "script echoes a CSS class".

Three incidental problems get fixed along the way:

1. **`pickachu-battery.sh` is half-broken today.** It echoes `80-percent-pikachu.png`,
   `60-percent-pikachu.png`, and `10-percent-pikachu.png`, but the files on disk are
   `80-percent-pickachu.png`, `60-percent-pikachi.png`, and `10-percent-pickachu.png`.
   Three of six battery states silently render nothing.
2. **Orphaned icons.** `network` hides itself when disconnected and `bluetooth` hides
   when disabled, but `image#network` / `image#bluetooth` stay onscreen regardless.
3. **Duplicate JSON key.** `config.jsonc:79-80` defines `"format-disconnected"` twice.

---

## Decisions (confirmed with user)

- Battery keeps its script, rewritten to emit JSON (`{"text":" ","class":"p80"}`) instead of a file path.
- Uniform icon height: **26px**. Bar `height` goes 34 → 38.
- Icons hide whenever their sibling module hides.
- Tooltips disabled on every module.
- All images consolidated into `assets/` and renamed consistently.

```
assets/pixelated-pokeball.png    → assets/pokeball.png
```

This directory is not a git repo, so plain `mv`, then `rmdir images/`.

## Step 2 — Rewrite `scripts/pickachu-battery.sh`

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh`

Emit waybar JSON instead of a path. `text` must be a single space — waybar's custom
module hides the widget when `text` is empty, and the space is what the background
image paints behind.

Requirements:

- `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`.
- Read `/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/capacity`. If the file is missing or unreadable,
  log to stderr and emit an empty `text` so the module hides rather than showing a
  stale sprite. Exit 0 regardless — a non-zero exit makes waybar respawn the module.
- Allow `WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY` to override the sysfs read, and `BATTERY_SYSFS` to
  override the path. These are what make all six branches testable without draining a
  battery (see Verification).
- Log the resolved capacity and chosen class to stderr with an ISO-8601 timestamp;
  waybar surfaces stderr in its own log, and stdout stays clean JSON.
- Same thresholds as today, so behavior is unchanged:

  | Capacity | Class |
  |---|---|
  | `> 80` | `p100` |
  | `> 60` | `p80` |
  | `> 40` | `p60` |
  | `> 20` | `p40` |
  | `> 10` | `p20` |
  | else | `p10` |

The `text` value carries no capacity number — the existing `battery` text module still
renders `{capacity}%` next to it.

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/config.jsonc`

### 3a. Bar height

`"height": 34` → `"height": 38`.

Box math per icon: 26px content + 2px padding × 2 + 4px margin × 2 = 38px.

### 3b. Replace the four `image#*` modules

Delete `image#clock`, `image#network`, `image#bluetooth`, `image#battery` entirely.
Replace them in `modules-left` / `modules-right` at the **same positions** (note
`image#battery` currently sits *after* the `battery` text module — preserve that):

| Old | New | Widget selector | Hides when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image#clock` | `custom/clock-icon` | `#custom-clock-icon` | never |
| `image#network` | `network#icon` | `#network.icon` | disconnected |
| `image#bluetooth` | `bluetooth#icon` | `#bluetooth.icon` | disabled |
| `image#battery` | `custom/battery-icon` | `#custom-battery-icon` | sysfs read fails |

**`custom/clock-icon`** — a static label, no `exec`. This mirrors the existing
`custom/divider` (`config.jsonc:41-43`), which already proves a `custom/` module with
only a `format` works:

```jsonc

  "format": " ",
  "tooltip": false,

```

**`network#icon`** — reusing the built-in `network` module (rather than a static
`custom/` one) is what makes the wooper disappear alongside the network text. An empty
`format-disconnected` is the same mechanism the existing `network` module already uses
to hide itself.

```jsonc
"network#icon": {
  "interface": "wlo1",
  "format": " ",
  "format-wifi": " ",
  "format-ethernet": " ",
```

**`bluetooth#icon`** — same idea, keyed on `format-disabled`:

The `#icon` suffix becomes a CSS class on the widget. This is the same mechanism
`hyprland/workspaces#taskbar` already relies on for its `#workspaces.taskbar` selector
(`style.css:43`), so the pattern is already proven in this config.

**`custom/battery-icon`**:

```jsonc
"custom/battery-icon": {
  "exec": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh",
  "return-type": "json",
  "interval": 30,
  "tooltip": false,

```

### 3c. Disable tooltips everywhere

Waybar has no global tooltip switch — it's per-module. Add `"tooltip": false` to
`clock`, `network`, `bluetooth`, `battery`, `hyprland/workspaces`,
`hyprland/workspaces#taskbar`, `custom/divider`, `custom/taskbar-divider`, and the four

means flipping `"tooltip": true` later restores the old text with no rework.

## Step 4 — Add the CSS

**File:** `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css`

Reuse the exact pattern from the existing pokeball rule (`style.css:22-35`):
`background-image` + `no-repeat` + `center` + `contain` + `background-origin: content-box`,
with the box sized by `min-width` / `min-height`.

`background-size: contain` fits the sprite *inside* the content box, so rendered height is
`min(box_height, box_width / aspect)`. For height to actually land on 26px, each box must
be at least `26 × aspect` wide:

| Selector | Sprite | Aspect | `min-width` | `min-height` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#custom-clock-icon` | `dialga.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#network.icon` | `wooper.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#bluetooth.icon` | `magneton.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |
| `#custom-battery-icon` | `pikachu-*.png` | 3.385:1 | **88px** | 26px |
| `#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active` | `pokeball.png` | 1:1 | 26px | 26px |

Structure it as one shared rule plus per-module `background-image` overrides, so the box
geometry lives in exactly one place:

```css
/* Shared geometry for every CSS-backed sprite. 26px content + 2px padding
   + 4px margin = 38px, matching the bar height. */
#custom-clock-icon,
#network.icon,
#bluetooth.icon,
#custom-battery-icon {
    background-position: center;
    background-repeat: no-repeat;
    background-size: contain;
    background-origin: content-box;
    color: transparent; /* hides the placeholder space glyph */
    min-width: 26px;
    min-height: 26px;
    padding: 2px;
    margin: 4px 0;
}

#custom-clock-icon { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/dialga.png'); }
#network.icon      { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/wooper.png'); }
#bluetooth.icon    { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/magneton.png'); }

/* 26px x 3.385 aspect ratio; contain letterboxes short without the full width */
#custom-battery-icon { min-width: 88px; }

#custom-battery-icon.p100 { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-100.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p80  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-80.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p60  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-60.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p40  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-40.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p20  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-20.png'); }
#custom-battery-icon.p10  { background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pikachu-10.png'); }
```

Also update the existing pokeball rule: point `background-image` at the renamed
`assets/pokeball.png`, and raise `min-width` / `min-height` from `22px` to `26px` so the
center pill's content height matches the left and right pills.

**Fallback if `contain` misbehaves:** GTK3 also accepts `background-size: auto 26px`,
which pins the height and derives width from the intrinsic aspect ratio, removing the
dependence on `min-width` being wide enough. Prefer `contain` since it's the pattern
already working in this file; switch only if the pikachu renders letterboxed.

`height` in waybar is a *request*, not a cap: GTK grows the window when content needs more
room. The `.modules-*` pills add `6px` margin + `4px` padding vertically (20px), so with a
38px icon box the pills want 58px. The bar is already in this state today (the pokeball's
34px box inside those same pills), so this is not a regression — but with icons 4px taller
than before, the bar will grow ~4px.

If the result is too tall, reduce `.modules-left/.modules-center/.modules-right`
`margin: 6px 4px` and `padding: 4px 8px` (`style.css:12-19`) rather than shrinking the
icons. Confirm visually in Verification step 5 before touching anything.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emits waybar JSON selecting a pikachu sprite via CSS class. The sprite itself
# lives in style.css as a background-image on #custom-battery-icon.<class>.
set -euo pipefail

BATTERY_SYSFS="${BATTERY_SYSFS:-/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/capacity}"

log() {
  printf '[%s] pickachu-battery: %s\n' "$(date -Iseconds)" "$*" >&2
}

# A single space, not an empty string: waybar hides a custom module whose text
# is empty, and the space is what the background image paints behind.
emit() {
  printf '{"text":"%s","class":"%s"}\n' "$1" "${2:-}"
}

capacity="${WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY:-}"

if [ -z "$capacity" ]; then
  if [ ! -r "$BATTERY_SYSFS" ]; then
    log "cannot read $BATTERY_SYSFS; hiding module"
    emit "" ""
    exit 0
  fi
  capacity=$(<"$BATTERY_SYSFS")
fi

if ! [[ "$capacity" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  log "non-numeric capacity '$capacity'; hiding module"
  emit "" ""
  exit 0
fi

if [ "$capacity" -gt 80 ]; then
  class=p100
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 60 ]; then
  class=p80
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 40 ]; then
  class=p60
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 20 ]; then
  class=p40
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 10 ]; then
  class=p20
else
  class=p10
fi

log "capacity=$capacity class=$class"
emit " " "$class"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emits waybar JSON selecting a pikachu sprite via CSS class. The sprite itself
# lives in style.css as a background-image on #custom-battery-icon.<class>.
set -euo pipefail

BATTERY_SYSFS="${BATTERY_SYSFS:-/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/capacity}"

log() {
  printf '[%s] pickachu-battery: %s\n' "$(date -Iseconds)" "$*" >&2
}

# A single space, not an empty string: waybar hides a custom module whose text
# is empty, and the space is what the background image paints behind.
emit() {
  printf '{"text":"%s","class":"%s"}\n' "$1" "$2"
}

capacity="${WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY:-}"

if [ -z "$capacity" ]; then
  if [ ! -r "$BATTERY_SYSFS" ]; then
    log "cannot read $BATTERY_SYSFS; hiding module"
    emit "" ""
    exit 0
  fi
  capacity=$(<"$BATTERY_SYSFS")
fi

if ! [[ "$capacity" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  log "non-numeric capacity '$capacity'; hiding module"
  emit "" ""
  exit 0
fi

if [ "$capacity" -gt 80 ]; then
  class=p100
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 60 ]; then
  class=p80
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 40 ]; then
  class=p60
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 20 ]; then
  class=p40
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 10 ]; then
  class=p20
else
  class=p10
fi

log "capacity=$capacity class=$class"
emit " " "$class"

| Script | Consumed as | Fields | Example |
|---|---|---|---|

| `workspace-tabs.sh` | `return-type: json` | `text` | `{"text":"│"}` |

cd ~/.config/waybar
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, sys

def strip_jsonc(s):
    out, i, n = [], 0, len(s)
    in_str = False
    while i < n:
        c = s[i]
        if in_str:
            out.append(c)
            if c == '\\' and i + 1 < n:
                out.append(s[i+1]); i += 2; continue
            if c == '"': in_str = False
            i += 1; continue
        if c == '"':
            in_str = True; out.append(c); i += 1; continue
        if c == '/' and i + 1 < n and s[i+1] == '/':
            while i < n and s[i] != '\n': i += 1
            continue
        if c == '/' and i + 1 < n and s[i+1] == '*':
            i += 2
            while i + 1 < n and not (s[i] == '*' and s[i+1] == '/'): i += 1
            i += 2; continue
        out.append(c); i += 1
    return ''.join(out)

def strip_trailing_commas(s):
    out, i, n, in_str = [], 0, len(s), False
    while i < n:
        c = s[i]
        if in_str:
            out.append(c)
            if c == '\\' and i+1 < n: out.append(s[i+1]); i += 2; continue
            if c == '"': in_str = False
            i += 1; continue
        if c == '"': in_str = True; out.append(c); i += 1; continue
        if c == ',':
            j = i + 1
            while j < n and s[j] in ' \t\r\n': j += 1
            if j < n and s[j] in '}]':
                i += 1; continue
        out.append(c); i += 1
    return ''.join(out)

src = open('config.jsonc').read()
try:
    cfg = json.loads(strip_trailing_commas(strip_jsonc(src)))
except Exception as e:
    print("PARSE ERROR:", e); sys.exit(1)

print("parsed ok; height =", cfg["height"])
mods = cfg["modules-left"] + cfg["modules-center"] + cfg["modules-right"]
print("\nmodule order:")
for section in ("modules-left","modules-center","modules-right"):
    print(f"  {section:16s} {cfg[section]}")

undefined = [m for m in mods if m not in cfg]
print("\nreferenced but undefined:", undefined or "none")
print("leftover image modules  :", [k for k in cfg if k.startswith("image")] or "none")

tips = [k for k,v in cfg.items() if isinstance(v,dict) and v.get("tooltip") is not False]
print("modules missing tooltip:false:", tips or "none")

# battery icon sits AFTER the battery text module, as before
r = cfg["modules-right"]
print("\nbattery icon after battery text:", r.index("custom/battery-icon") > r.index("battery"))

import json, sys

def strip_jsonc(s):
    out, i, n = [], 0, len(s)
    in_str = False
    while i < n:
        c = s[i]
        if in_str:
            out.append(c)
            if c == '\\' and i + 1 < n:
                out.append(s[i+1]); i += 2; continue
            if c == '"': in_str = False
            i += 1; continue
        if c == '"':
            in_str = True; out.append(c); i += 1; continue
        if c == '/' and i + 1 < n and s[i+1] == '/':
            while i < n and s[i] != '\n': i += 1
            continue
        if c == '/' and i + 1 < n and s[i+1] == '*':
            i += 2
            while i + 1 < n and not (s[i] == '*' and s[i+1] == '/'): i += 1
            i += 2; continue
        out.append(c); i += 1
    return ''.join(out)

def strip_trailing_commas(s):
    out, i, n, in_str = [], 0, len(s), False
    while i < n:
        c = s[i]
        if in_str:
            out.append(c)
            if c == '\\' and i+1 < n: out.append(s[i+1]); i += 2; continue
            if c == '"': in_str = False
            i += 1; continue
        if c == '"': in_str = True; out.append(c); i += 1; continue
        if c == ',':
            j = i + 1
            while j < n and s[j] in ' \t\r\n': j += 1
            if j < n and s[j] in '}]':
                i += 1; continue
        out.append(c); i += 1
    return ''.join(out)

Old bar was **56px** tall despite `height: 34` — waybar had already grown it. The new one wants 60. So `height: 38` from the plan is simply wrong, and left alone the bar would grow 4px taller than you have now.

Plan Step 5 anticipated this and said to trim the pill margins rather than shrink the icons. Let me measure both options in the scratchpad instead of guessing.

input.command:
cd /tmp/claude-1000/-home-krubics--config-waybar/34ff1c20-f076-46fc-b02c-44b1662a5db5/scratchpad

probe() { # $1 = pill margin px, $2 = requested height
  sed "s/margin: 6px 4px;/margin: ${1}px 4px;/" new-style.css > probe-style.css
  sed "s/\"height\": 38,/\"height\": $2,/" new-config.jsonc > probe-config.jsonc
  timeout 4 waybar -c probe-config.jsonc -s probe-style.css -l warning > probe.log 2>&1
  local min
  min=$(grep -oE 'minimum height: [0-9]+' probe.log | tail -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
  printf '  pill margin %spx, requested %-3s -> %s\n' "$1" "$2" \
    "${min:+needs ${min}px}${min:-no warning, fits at ${2}px}"
}

echo "=== how tall does the bar actually need to be? ==="
probe 6 38
probe 6 60
probe 4 38
probe 4 56
probe 4 54
probe 2 52

python3 - <<'PY'
from PIL import Image
im = Image.open('bar-full.png').convert('RGB')
W,H = im.size
px = im.load()

# pill background = most common colour inside a pill (sample a blank strip)
from collections import Counter
bg = Counter(px[x,H//2] for x in range(200,260)).most_common(1)[0][0]
def differs(c, t=40):
    return sum(abs(a-b) for a,b in zip(c,bg)) > t

# columns that contain any non-background pixel
cols = [any(differs(px[x,y]) for y in range(H)) for x in range(W)]
segs, run = [], None
for x,on in enumerate(cols):
    if on and run is None: run = x
    elif not on and run is not None:
        if x-run >= 6: segs.append((run,x-1))
        run = None

def vext(x0,x1):
    rows=[y for y in range(H) if any(differs(px[x,y]) for x in range(x0,x1+1))]
    return (min(rows), max(rows), max(rows)-min(rows)+1) if rows else (0,0,0)

print(f"pill bg={bg}  bar={W}x{H}\n")
print(f"{'x-range':>14} {'w':>4} {'top':>4} {'bot':>4} {'height':>6}")
for a,b in segs:
    t,bt,h = vext(a,b)
    print(f"{a:>6}-{b:<7} {b-a+1:>4} {t:>4} {bt:>4} {h:>6}")

content.text: All four sprites now sit in identical 26px boxes — but the *visible* pokemon inside them are not the same height. Let me check why.

input.command:
cd ~/.config/waybar/assets
echo "sprite            canvas      ink bbox (alpha-trimmed)   ink%h   ink h @26px box"
for f in dialga.png wooper.png magneton.png pikachu-100.png pokeball.png; do
  canvas=$(identify -format '%wx%h' "$f")
  ch=${canvas#*x}; cw=${canvas%x*}
  bbox=$(convert "$f" -trim -format '%wx%h' info: 2>/dev/null)
  bh=${bbox#*x}
  pct=$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.0f\", $bh*100/$ch}")
  # contain into a 26px-tall box: rendered ink height = 26 * (ink_h / canvas_h)
  ink=$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.1f\", 26*$bh/$ch}")
  printf '%-16s %-11s %-24s %4s%%   %s px\n' "$f" "$canvas" "$bbox" "$pct" "$ink"
done

lastPrompt: Let's convert all my jsonc image modules into use background images styled in css instead just like the pokeball example so we can have a consistent height of all the different pokemon.

content.text:
Here's the real obstacle. Equal boxes ≠ equal pokemon, because each PNG carries a different amount of transparent margin:

| sprite | canvas | ink fills | pokemon height in a 26px box |
|---|---|---|---|
| dialga | 800×800 | 82% | **21.3px** |
| magneton | 364×364 | 68% | **17.6px** |
| pikachu | 677×200 | 63% | **16.4px** |
| wooper | 256×256 | 47% | **12.2px** |

Wooper renders at barely half dialga's height. The boxes are uniform; the pokemon aren't. Fixing this means trimming the transparent border off the PNGs — which overwrites your only copies, so let me check one thing before proposing it.

input.command:
cd ~/.config/waybar/assets
echo "=== do all 6 pikachu gauge frames share an ink bbox? (they must, or the gauge jitters) ==="
for f in pikachu-100.png pikachu-80.png pikachu-60.png pikachu-40.png pikachu-20.png pikachu-10.png; do
  printf '%-16s canvas=%-9s ink=%-10s offset=%s\n' "$f" \
    "$(identify -format '%wx%h' "$f")" \
    "$(convert "$f" -trim -format '%wx%h' info:)" \
    "$(convert "$f" -trim -format '%X%Y' info:)"
done
echo
echo "=== union bbox across all 6 (what a safe common trim would be) ==="
convert pikachu-*.png -flatten -trim -format 'union ink = %wx%h at %X%Y\n' info: 2>/dev/null | head -1
input.description: Check pikachu frame bboxes for consistency

lastPrompt: Let's convert all my jsonc image modules into use background images styled in css instead just like the pokeball example so we can have a consistent height of all the different pokemon.

content.text:
All six gauge frames share the same ink box (`628×126 at +33+34`), so a single common crop trims them without making the gauge jitter as the battery drains. That means trimming is safe.

Two consequences worth your call before I touch the PNGs:

questions.question: Trim the transparent margins so the pokemon themselves are the same height?

options.label: Trim all, incl. pokeball (Recommended)
options.description: Alpha-trim every sprite to its ink bbox (one shared crop for the 6 gauge frames). Every pokemon then renders at a true 26px tall. Pokeball grows 19.5px → 26px, so it fills the accent pill more. I'll copy the untrimmed originals to assets/original/ first, so it's fully reversible.
options.preview:
before (26px box)      after trim
dialga    21.3px  ->  26px
magneton  17.6px  ->  26px
pikachu   16.4px  ->  26px
wooper    12.2px  ->  26px
pokeball  19.5px  ->  26px

options.label: Trim pokemon, leave pokeball
options.description: Same, but pokeball keeps its current transparent margin and stays 19.5px inside its blue pill. The four pokemon become uniform at 26px; the pokeball reads slightly smaller than them.
options.preview:
before (26px box)      after trim
dialga    21.3px  ->  26px
magneton  17.6px  ->  26px
pikachu   16.4px  ->  26px
wooper    12.2px  ->  26px
pokeball  19.5px  ->  19.5px (unchanged)

options.label: Don't touch the PNGs
options.description: Stop here. The CSS conversion is done and every icon box is a uniform 26px, but the pokemon inside those boxes stay at their current mismatched sizes (wooper renders about half of dialga's height) because that padding is baked into the image files.

questions.question: Trimming makes the battery gauge's aspect ratio 4.99:1, so at 26px tall it needs 130px of width (it's 88px now, and was 115px before this change). OK?

options.label: Yes, let it widen to 130px (Recommended)
options.description: Each of the 5 pikachu cells then renders about 26×26, matching the other pokemon exactly. Costs ~42px of bar width out of 2560.

options.label: Keep it at 88px
options.description: Cap the gauge box at 88px wide. background-size: contain then letterboxes it, so the pikachus render ~17.6px tall — shorter than the other pokemon. Saves width, reintroduces the height mismatch for battery only.

options.label: Shrink all icons instead
options.description: Drop the shared box from 26px to ~22px so the widened gauge costs less width (110px). All pokemon stay uniform, just smaller. The bar could then also get shorter.

lastPrompt: Let's convert all my jsonc image modules into use background images styled in css instead just like the pokeball example so we can have a consistent height of all the different pokemon.

content.text: Trimming all sprites, originals backed up first.

input.command:
cd ~/.config/waybar/assets
mkdir -p original && cp *.png original/ && echo "originals backed up to assets/original/ ($(ls original | wc -l) files)"
echo
# Gauge frames share one crop so the 5-cell strip never shifts between states.
for f in pikachu-100.png pikachu-80.png pikachu-60.png pikachu-40.png pikachu-20.png pikachu-10.png; do
  convert "$f" -crop 629x126+33+34 +repage "$f"
done
# Square icons trim to their own ink.
for f in dialga.png wooper.png magneton.png pokeball.png; do
  convert "$f" -trim +repage "$f"
done
echo "sprite            canvas     aspect   width @26px box"
for f in dialga.png wooper.png magneton.png pokeball.png pikachu-100.png; do
  read w h <<<"$(identify -format '%w %h' "$f")"
  printf '%-16s %-10s %-8s %s px\n' "$f" "${w}x${h}" \
    "$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.3f\", $w/$h}")" \
    "$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.0f\", 26*$w/$h}")"
done
echo
echo "=== all 6 gauge frames identical canvas? ==="
identify -format '%f %wx%h\n' pikachu-*.png
